subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should manual `cron run` be a fully non-consuming verification path across delete-after-run, counters, retry/backoff, failure alerts, and schedule recompute state?
rationale: The code fix can be repaired mechanically, but the permanent user-facing contract changes manual cron semantics beyond the original deletion gate and needs maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Accept full non-consuming manual runs
options.body: After the backoff repair, manual runs record their own outcome while leaving scheduled deletion, counters, alerts, and next-run scheduling to the timer path.

options.title: Narrow to one-shot deletion only
options.body: Limit this PR to preventing manual `deleteAfterRun` consumption and keep counter/backoff/alert semantics closer to current behavior.

options.title: Reject the behavior change
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep manual runs consuming scheduled state until a different cron UX contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Accept full non-consuming manual runs
recommendation.body: After the backoff repair, manual runs record their own outcome while leaving scheduled deletion, counters, alerts, and next-run scheduling to the timer path.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the listed project lead and has recent cron protocol/status ownership history, making him the strongest available product-contract owner.
